entities.summary:
Tomaso da Modena (fl. 1340-1379) was a mid-14th-century Italian painter of the Modena school, known for his contributions to the development of the 'Gothic style' in Renaissance art. His most famous works include 'The Virgin and Child with Saint Catherine' and 'The Portrait of a Young Man'.

Da Modena's artistic style was influenced by the works of Giotto and the Byzantine tradition, and he is considered one of the greatest painters of the 14th century.

His legacy can be seen in the works of later Renaissance artists, such as Sandro Botticelli and Fra Angelico, who were influenced by his innovative use of color and composition.

In the words of the art historian Giorgio Vasari, 'Tomaso da Modena was a great painter, who, in his time, was considered the greatest of all' ('Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects', 1568).

Despite his significance in the development of Renaissance art, Tomaso da Modena's life and works remain relatively unknown to the general public.
